title: Transnational relational resilience: ‘ Souvenir de Syrie ’ as mnemonic artistic renderings in Romania
abstract: The paper zooms in on parallel memories of migration and displacement enacted in Romanian art after 1989, with a focus on Dan Acostioaei’s body of artistic memory work. The focus is on drawing parallels between two phenomena: on the one hand, the migration mobility of the labour force from communist Romania to the Middle East (in the 1970s and 1980s) and, on the other hand, the massive work-related migration after 1989 to the West. The exploration moves beyond regional ‘mnemonic diplomacy’ and focuses on transnationally distant constellations of memory alliances. The research employed photo-elicitation and interviews as a point of departure for prompting memories of movement and uprootedness. By drawing parallels between multi-folded memories of migration/displacement, the paper aims to explore how ‘working through’ past emergencies act as a coping strategy in the wake of the Syrian refugee crisis (2011–2024). The argument revolves around how art can foster transnational relational mnemonic resilience.
